render-tests/fill-extrusion-pattern/glob: On Mesa 26.0.8's lavapipe and on llvmpipe's OpenGL, which CI draws on, the depth that the extrusion's depth pass writes and the depth its color pass tests (less or equal) disagree on part of the diamond's walls, so those pixels show what is behind them. Raising heights on GL JS's mean-radius sphere moved which pixels: 337 of 131072 differ on lavapipe and 455 on llvmpipe (Mesa 26.0.8 and 26.2.5), where 262 (0.2%) are allowed; on the WGS84 radius, 198 and 226. RADV (171) and Mesa 26.2.5's lavapipe (169) draw the walls whole and pass
gljs/render-tests/projection/globe/terra: Mesa 26.0.8's lavapipe puts the checkers' edges where RADV does, to 0.01 px, but samples the drapes a little softer: a pixel inside a square next to an edge comes out 5% grey where RADV's is black. Against GL JS's picture, which sits 0.1 px off ours (the globe's camera), pixelmatch then counts 1663 of 65536 px rather than RADV's 240, where 242 are allowed
